advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the blue-green 2x-overlap (old+new mcp both mounting gerrit_mcp_tickets read-write) with the commit's single-writer rationale, or document why concurrent mcp writers on one store is acceptable.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:365-369 mcp_run_new adds `-e "REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets"` and `-v "gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets"`

autodeploy.sh:676 comment `# 4. start the NEW container ALONGSIDE the old.` and stop_grace 1260s in docker-compose.yml:329 mean the OLD mcp container keeps writing in-flight certified-op events while the NEW one boots

commit body: 'A dedicated volume rather than sharing reviewbot-tickets: the write lock would serialize two writers, but that store was provisioned for one and nothing in its design anticipates a second.' — yet blue-green runs two mcp writers on gerrit_mcp_tickets simultaneously
reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:125 uses `lock.write_lock(...)`, confirming the store relies on a write lock to serialize writers
advisory.finding: The mcp service is deployed blue-green (autodeploy.sh starts the NEW container alongside the retiring OLD one under a 1260s stop grace), and both containers mount the same read-write `gerrit_mcp_tickets` volume and emit ticket events. This creates two concurrent MCP writers against one store during every cutover — the exact concurrent-writer scenario the commit's dedicated-volume rationale claims to avoid ('that store was provisioned for one').
scenarios: Every blue-green mcp redeploy: old container finishes a certified op (writes a ticket event) while the new container also begins writing to the same volume
Two certified ops racing across old+new containers contend on the store write lock, serializing/stalling one behind the other

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always" on the mcp service (and mcp_run_new) to match the review-bot sibling, or note explicitly why the mcp store relies on the implicit default.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:120 (reviewbot service) `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"` is set explicitly
docker-compose.yml:333-371 mcp `environment:` block sets no REBAR_SYNC_PUSH
README.md:355 and src/rebar/_store/push.py:4 document `always` as the default, so mcp auto-push still functions
Dockerfile.mcp:73 comment: 'so writes accumulate + auto-push instead of living in an ephemeral dir'
advisory.finding: The commit body and Dockerfile.mcp comment describe the store as read-write with 'auto-push', but neither the mcp compose env, mcp_run_new, nor Dockerfile.mcp sets REBAR_SYNC_PUSH, whereas the sibling review-bot compose service pins REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always" explicitly. Auto-push works only because 'always' is the implicit default; the divergence from the sibling makes the push behavior rely on an unstated default.
scenarios: An operator later sets sync.push in a config file or env for the box and unexpectedly changes mcp push behavior because it was never pinned like the sibling

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Set safe.directory (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets) on the mcp service, mirroring the review-bot's dubious-ownership workaround.
evidence: Review-bot precedent, docker-compose.yml:130-141: 'The container runs as root ... but that named volume is owned uid 1000 ... so git's dubious-ownership guard (>=2.35.2) refused EVERY op on it ... making 100% of code_review artifact emissions fail (ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR)' followed by GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0=safe.directory/VALUE_0=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets
The mcp service block (docker-compose.yml:361-392) adds REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, MCP_TICKETS_PAT, and the gerrit_mcp_tickets mount but NO GIT_CONFIG_*/safe.directory entry for /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets
reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh runs `git -C "$DIR" config`, `git fetch`, `git reset --hard`, and rebar runtime does git commit/push against the same volume (reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:52-176)
Review-bot pins it: docker-compose.yml:120 `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "always"` with the comment 'auto-push every code_review artifact ticket event to origin/tickets as it is written'
docs/config.md:197 'sync.push = "always" ... (env REBAR_SYNC_PUSH)' — default is always, so behavior is currently correct
The mcp service environment block (docker-compose.yml:361-371) sets REBAR_TRACKER_DIR and MCP_TICKETS_PAT but not REBAR_SYNC_PUSH
advisory.finding: The mcp compose service mounts and writes to the gerrit_mcp_tickets named volume but does not set the git `safe.directory` (GIT_CONFIG_*) workaround the review-bot service required for its identically-provisioned tickets volume; if the volume ends up owned by a uid other than the container's root, git's dubious-ownership guard will refuse every clone/fetch/commit/push, breaking the store exactly as documented for the review-bot.
merged_from: The mcp service relies on the implicit REBAR_SYNC_PUSH default ('always') to auto-push ticket events, whereas the review-bot service pins it explicitly; the deliberate pattern-mirroring is incomplete, leaving the store's push behavior undocumented and undefended against a future default change.
scenarios: gerrit_mcp_tickets is created by compose-up.sh as a bind volume whose backing dir is owned by a uid != container root, tripping git's >=2.35.2 dubious-ownership guard
advisory.suggested_fix: Add to the mcp service `environment:` the same guard the review-bot uses: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: "1", GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: "safe.directory", GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: "/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets" (and mirror it in autodeploy.sh's mcp_run_new `-e` flags).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the safe.directory GIT_CONFIG_* `-e` flags to autodeploy.sh mcp_run_new so blue-green containers match the compose git-ownership guard.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:347-370 mcp_run_new adds `-e REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` and `-v gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` but no GIT_CONFIG_* safe.directory `-e` flags
The compose-parity test (test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py) asserts docker-run reproduces the compose env EXACTLY, so any safe.directory added to compose must also be added here
advisory.finding: The autodeploy blue-green `mcp_run_new` docker-run path does not carry the GIT_CONFIG_* safe.directory guard either, so even if the compose service is fixed, redeployed (docker run) containers would still hit the dubious-ownership failure against gerrit_mcp_tickets.
scenarios: A blue-green redeploy runs the mcp container via `docker run` with a uid-mismatched gerrit_mcp_tickets volume

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Dockerfile.mcp entrypoint comment to say the credential helper is URL-KEYED but written to --global config (not 'not --global'), or scope it non-globally.
evidence: Dockerfile.mcp:70 comment: 'Configure a PER-URL (not --global) git credential helper for the tickets remote'
Dockerfile.mcp:88 code: echo '  git config --global "credential.${MCP_TICKETS_URL}.helper" ...'
Same discrepancy exists verbatim in Dockerfile.reviewbot:134 vs :150, so it is an inherited comment inaccuracy
advisory.finding: The Dockerfile.mcp entrypoint comment claims a 'PER-URL (not --global) git credential helper ... so the ... PAT never lands on disk', but the generated code configures the helper with `git config --global`; the helper is URL-keyed yet globally scoped, contradicting the stated 'not --global' intent.
scenarios: A reader relying on the comment assumes the helper is scoped away from the container's other git repos

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that materializes and executes the generated mcp-entrypoint.sh (as tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_entrypoint.py does for the review-bot) asserting returncode 0 and that `exec "$@"` still runs when the PAT is unset, when `git clone` fails, and when the ensure script fails.
evidence: Added entrypoint at infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:83-103 generates a shell script whose soft paths are added lines: `git clone ... || echo "mcp: tickets store clone deferred"` (line 92-93), `sh /app/infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh ... || echo "mcp: tickets store ensure deferred"` (line 99-100), and the unconditional `exec "$@"` (line 101).

Dockerfile.mcp:78-80 declares this as the design point: 'FAILURE POSTURE IS SOFT: no PAT, or a failed clone/ensure, must NOT stop the container booting ... it is not exercised by the in-repo unit tests.'

The only entrypoint test (tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:291-301) asserts only text substrings via `_DOCKERFILE.read_text()`; it never materializes or executes the generated script, so it cannot observe boot success/failure.

A directly-applicable behavioral harness already exists: tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_entrypoint.py:14-56 materializes the sibling Dockerfile.reviewbot entrypoint with fake `git`/`reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` and asserts `result.returncode == 0` and the ensure+app ordering with the PAT unset — exactly the contract the MCP entrypoint mirrors.

Named violating input: an edit that changes `git clone ... || echo ...` (Dockerfile.mcp:92-93) to drop the `|| echo` fallthrough — under the entrypoint's `set -e`, a clone failure would then abort boot instead of deferring, yet the text-grep test stays green because the substring `git clone --single-branch --branch tickets` is still present.

tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:294-301 asserts literal source strings: `assert "git clone --single-branch --branch tickets" in text`, `assert "reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh" in text`, `assert 'CMD ["rebar-mcp"]' in text`.

The grepped artifact is the executable image build recipe / generated shell script (infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp), not a non-executable instruction manifest — so this is source-grepping, not a Rule-5 structural grep.
Rule-4 litmus: renaming the branch to a variable, reordering the clone flags, or extracting the clone into a helper would break these assertions with zero observable-behavior change.
dropped.finding: The newly-added Dockerfile.mcp entrypoint's SOFT failure posture — no PAT / failed clone / failed ensure must all still let the container boot (exec "$@") — is entirely untested; the only entrypoint test greps the Dockerfile text and cannot detect a regression that makes any of these paths abort boot.
merged_from: test_dockerfile_mcp_entrypoint_provisions_the_ticket_store asserts substrings against the executable Dockerfile source-under-test, making it a change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving edit to the generated entrypoint while providing no behavioral coverage.
scenarios: A future edit removes/alters the `|| echo` fallthrough on the clone or ensure line and, under `set -e`, a deferred clone or ensure failure now kills container boot — violating the SOFT posture the commit deliberately introduced.
MCP_TICKETS_PAT unset: the whole `if [ -n ...]` block is skipped and only ensure + exec run; no test verifies the container still boots in this canary state.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add tests mirroring test_reviewbot_entrypoint.py: extract the RUN heredoc for /usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh, materialize it into tmp_path, put fake `git` (exit 1) and fake `reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh` (exit 1) on PATH, run it as `entrypoint sh -c 'echo app >> receipt'` with and without MCP_TICKETS_PAT, and assert returncode 0 plus that the app command ran (soft posture holds through both failure and no-PAT cases).
